data.body:
Landed as Gerrit change 1625 (LLM-Review +1, Verified +1, submitted and merged to main).

Delivered, per the re-scope: coverage['metrics']['verification_recorded'] in _attach_code_review_metrics, plus a WARNING naming the missing count when it is false. The predicate counts only findings actually expected to carry a Pass-2 block (tier == 'LLM' and not indeterminate/no-verification), so DET-tier detector findings and deliberate no-verification degradations cannot pin the signal to false on routine runs. It also stays quiet when the verifier made zero requests, leaving that outage to grounding_health rather than double-counting it. Advisory only - it never touches verdict['verdict'], and the new metrics key is additive for schema-tolerant readers. The module-level logger it needs supersedes two function-local loggers, now removed.

Six new tests: recorded-true on a healthy verdict, recorded-false with the warning, the DET-tier/indeterminate false-alarm guard, the zero-verifier-request case, the advisory/surfaced double-count guard, and a sidecar round-trip pin asserting {binary, severity_attributes} survives build_payload in all four buckets. RED was verified before landing: five of the six fail with KeyError('verification_recorded') against the pre-change source; the sixth is the regression pin and is correctly green either way.

All four ACs re-verified against the landed tree: test_code_review_fp_ledger.py 20 passed; -k 'code_review or sidecar' 464 passed, 3 skipped; -k 'sidecar' 104 passed, 3 skipped. make lint and make typecheck clean (502 source files).

CI note for the record: patchset 1 took Verified -1 from version skew, not a defect - the mutation workflow resolves at main's ref and invoked 'mutation_gate.py select', a subcommand the patchset's older base predated, so recheck could not have fixed it. A rebase onto fresh origin/main resolved it and patchset 2 went green.

Closing as 'preexisting': the missing error signal was a longstanding gap dating to the code-review gate's own construction, not a regression from any recent change. Note that item 1 of the original filing was withdrawn - the audit recorded above disproved it, and the verification blocks it asked to persist were already being persisted.
